data.name: readtime
data.tagline: The estimate readers check before they commit to a paragraph.
data.headline: Tell them what they're signing up for before they scroll.
data.sub: readtime counts words at publish time and writes the estimate straight into your post's metadata. No client-side JavaScript, no recalculating on every page view. Four display variants, three sizes, every value bound to a CSS token.
data.home_card_copy: Readers check the estimate before they read the paragraph.
data.pairs_note: someone who finishes a post is your best candidate to share it or heart it. readtime runs before either of those decisions gets made.
data.demo_caption: 5 min read - 1,240 words, computed once at publish, served instantly.
data.setup_note: Every published post gets a reading time automatically. Older posts pick it up the next time you hit publish.

data.name: callout
data.tagline: The block every technical writer reaches for, and most CMSes never ship.
data.headline: The block readers actually stop and read.
data.sub: callout registers a native Portable Text block for info, warning, tip, and danger. It shows up in the EmDash editor like any other block, and Callout.astro ships with defaults that look designed, not bolted on. Every visual value is a CSS custom property.
data.home_card_copy: Info, warning, tip, danger - four callouts, one native editor block.
data.pairs_note: callouts and code blocks are the two things a technical writer reaches for first.
data.setup_note: The callout block shows up in your EmDash editor immediately. Wire the component into your layout once, and every callout in every post renders correctly from then on.

data.name: sharepost
data.tagline: If a reader wants to share your post, that should take one click.
data.headline: Make sharing the obvious next move.
data.sub: sharepost generates correct share URLs for X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Bluesky, and email on every publish, then renders them as circular icon buttons. No JavaScript SDKs, no tracking pixels, no 200KB of vendor script for five links.
data.home_card_copy: Correct share URLs for five platforms, computed once, at publish.
data.pairs_note: a share and a heart are different signals from different readers. Run both, and you stop guessing which one you're missing.
data.demo_caption: Circular by default, no configuration, correct in both themes.
data.setup_note: Every published post has share URLs the moment it goes live. Add the component once, and every future post inherits it.

data.name: heartpost
data.tagline: The lightest thing a reader can do to tell you they liked it.
data.headline: One click, no account, and it still counts.
data.sub: heartpost stores a heart count in Cloudflare KV and updates it with an optimistic client-side increment, so the number moves before the network round-trip finishes. HeartButton.astro ships in four variants, fully restyled through CSS custom properties.
data.home_card_copy: One click, no account, counted in KV.
data.pairs_note: a heart is a quiet yes. A share is a loud one. Run both and you can tell which post readers loved versus which one they wanted other people to see.
data.demo_caption: The count moves the instant you click, before KV even confirms it.
data.setup_note: Every post gets a heart count the moment you add the component. No account system to stand up, no cookies to manage.

data.name: shortlink
data.tagline: A clean URL for every post, generated the moment you publish.
data.headline: The link you'd actually want to paste in a tweet.
data.sub: shortlink generates a short URL for every published post and stores it in Cloudflare KV. CopyLink.astro ships in three variants - circle, pill, inline - with a green check on copy that resets itself after two seconds.
data.home_card_copy: Copy the link in one click. No dashboard, no separate service.
data.pairs_note: shortlink, sharepost, and heartpost are the three things a reader can do without leaving the page. Most posts ship all three.
data.demo_caption: Click to copy - a green check confirms it, then fades after two seconds.
data.setup_note: Every published post gets a short URL automatically, no separate step. The component handles the clipboard copy.

data.name: tocgen
data.tagline: A 3,000-word post without a table of contents is a post nobody finishes.
data.headline: Show readers the shape of the post before they commit to it.
data.sub: tocgen parses headings out of your Portable Text content at publish time and writes a nested navigation tree into the post's metadata. TableOfContents.astro renders it with a sticky sidebar variant that tracks scroll position. Posts under the heading threshold are skipped automatically.
data.home_card_copy: A table of contents, generated from your headings, skipped on short posts.
data.pairs_note: readtime tells a reader how long the post is. tocgen shows them the shape of it. Together they answer the two questions a reader asks before committing: how long, and about what.
data.demo_caption: Sticky on desktop, nested h2/h3, active section highlighted as you scroll.
data.setup_note: Every post with three or more headings gets a table of contents automatically. Shorter posts are skipped - nothing to configure.

data.name: engage
data.tagline: heartpost, sharepost, and shortlink, wired into one component.
data.headline: Three plugins, one import, one row under every post.
data.sub: engage composes heartpost, sharepost, and shortlink into a single EngagementBar.astro. Install the three underlying plugins, then import the bundle instead of stitching the components together yourself.
data.home_card_copy: One row under every post: heart, share, copy link.
data.pairs_note: engage wraps heartpost, sharepost, and shortlink. Install all three plugins, then use engage's component instead of assembling your own layout.
data.demo_caption: Heart, share buttons, and copy link, rendered from one component.
data.setup_note: engage is a bundle, not a plugin of its own. Register heartpost, sharepost, and shortlink, then import EngagementBar.astro from @plugdash/engage into your Post layout.

data.name: autobuild
data.tagline: Hit publish in the admin. The deploy is already running.
data.headline: The admin panel that also deploys your site.
data.sub: autobuild fires your Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or Vercel build hook on every publish - no git push, no manual redeploy. It debounces for five seconds, so a batch of edits triggers one deploy instead of ten.
data.home_card_copy: The plugin that makes the admin the thing that ships the site.
data.pairs_note: readtime and tocgen write metadata on publish. autobuild is what gets that metadata onto the live site within a minute, instead of at the next scheduled build.
data.demo_caption: Publish in the admin and the build hook fires - four lines of config, no git push.
data.setup_note: Paste your build hook URL from Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or Vercel as an env var. Every publish rebuilds the site after that, debounced so a burst of edits fires one deploy, not ten.

data.name: socialcard
data.tagline: The preview image that decides whether anyone clicks the link at all.
data.headline: Generate the card before anyone hits share.
data.sub: socialcard renders an OG image with Satori the moment you publish, then converts it to PNG with resvg-js - both running inside the same Cloudflare Worker that serves the rest of your site. No screenshot service, no third-party API key, no cold start. Three templates ship built in, every colour and font is config, not code.
data.home_card_copy: The OG image renders in the Worker, at publish, not through a screenshot service.
data.pairs_note: sharepost puts the link in front of people. socialcard is what they see before they click it - the two only work as a pair.
data.demo_caption: 1200x630 PNG, rendered from Satori JSX, generated once per publish.
data.setup_note: Publish a post and the card exists at metadata.ogImage before the deploy even finishes. Point your layout's og:image meta tag at it once and every future post inherits it.

data.name: fromsubstack
data.tagline: The export button Substack gives you, turned into a working blog somewhere else.
data.headline: Point it at the export ZIP. Walk away with a working blog.
data.sub: fromsubstack unzips a Substack export, converts each post's HTML into Portable Text, and re-uploads every image to your own media library. Slugs carry over by default, so old links from newsletters and search results keep resolving. Everything lands as a draft first - nothing goes live until you review it.
data.home_card_copy: Unzip the Substack export, get EmDash content back - posts, images, slugs intact.
data.hooks: none - runs as a one-time CLI import
data.config_example:
// runs via CLI, not the plugins array:
npx emdash plugin fromsubstack --file export.zip --status draft
data.pairs_note: if the old Substack URLs are indexed anywhere, redirects is what keeps them from turning into 404s once the archive moves.
data.demo_caption: 5 posts, 3 with images, imported and re-hosted in one CLI run.
data.setup_note: Export your archive from Substack's settings, then run the import command with the ZIP path. Re-running the same file skips posts it's already imported instead of duplicating them.

data.name: redirects
data.tagline: Change a slug and the old URL still has to go somewhere.
data.headline: Rename a post without breaking the link everyone already has.
data.sub: redirects watches every slug change and writes a 301 automatically, no extra step. Every request gets checked against the redirect table before your site ever renders a page, and a hit counter tracks which old URLs are still getting traffic. A CSV importer handles the bulk redirects you bring over from a migration.
data.home_card_copy: Change a slug, get a 301 automatically. No dead links from a rename.
data.pairs_note: a migration brings a list of URLs that used to work somewhere else. redirects is what makes them keep working here.
data.demo_caption: Rename a slug, and the old path 301s to the new one before the next request.
data.setup_note: Install it and slug changes start redirecting immediately. Bring over redirects from an old CMS with the CSV importer on the admin page instead of typing each one in by hand.

data.title: The PlugDash launch: eight plugins, one live site
data.description: Announcing PlugDash: eight MIT-licensed plugins for EmDash, all installed on the catalog site itself.

children.text: Today PlugDash ships with eight plugins for EmDash, all MIT-licensed, all on npm, and all installed on the site you're reading right now.

PlugDash is a plugin catalog for EmDash, the open-source CMS built on Astro and Cloudflare. Each plugin in the catalog solves a small, specific problem your blog has on day one - reading time, share buttons, a heart counter, short links, a table of contents, callouts, and publish-triggered rebuilds.

Every plugin ships with a companion Astro component. You install the plugin, add one import to your layout, and your readers see the result. No configuration needed to ship something good. Full CSS token customisation when you want to change the look.
generates share URLs for X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Bluesky, and email.
gives every post a short URL.
parses headings and writes a nested table of contents.
adds info, warning, tip, and danger blocks to the Portable Text editor.
bundles heart, share, and copy into one component.
fires a deploy hook on publish so the admin becomes the thing that moves the site.
Why the site runs on EmDash

plugdash.dev runs on EmDash with all eight plugins registered and active, because a catalog that doesn't use its own plugins is just a brochure. The reading time on this post, the engagement bar at the bottom, the table of contents sidebar on desktop, the callout blocks - all of them are live plugins running on this page. The site is the proof.
The next batch focuses on migration and interop.
lets you move a Substack archive into EmDash in one step.
export your EmDash content back out - the anti-lock-in pair. After that:
We hold everything we ship to the same bar as these eight: small enough to read in one sitting, open enough to fork, and live on plugdash.dev before we ever ask you to install it.
